[2026 Adamuz rail disaster] On 18 January 2026, an Iryo high-speed train derailed in the municipality of Adamuz, in the province of Córdoba, Spain. A second train, Renfe Alvia 2384, crashed into it and was also derailed. The incident killed 46 people, including the Renfe train driver, and injured 292 others, 15 critically. The crash was Spain's worst railway disaster since the Santiago de Compostela derailment in 2013, and was the fourth deadliest railway accident in Spain until 10 months later, when at least 69 people died in the October 2026 Toledo train collision. A preliminary investigation by the Civil Guard found that a poor weld with an improper kit had caused rail breakage, and was compounded by poor data collection practices, inexperienced track inspectors, and overly relaxed programming of track circuit-connected alert systems. The line reopened for service on 17 February 2026 after a month of repairs and testing.
